The driver's GPS trace confirms which route was actually taken and when — the vehicle left the recommended PIE line at 18:45:16 and rejoined it at Loyang Avenue / Upper Changi Road North at 19:01:07, travelling via New Upper Changi Road and Upper Changi Road North — but POL-RD-22 forbids re-measuring the route from the trace because a sparse trace understates its length (this trace measures only 21.24 km, below the recommended 23.20 km), so the driver cannot use the trace to argue the deviation was within tolerance; the recorded 1.90 km stands.

The reroute is not traffic-justified. The traffic advisory for this trip, EV-ADVIS-06008-01, is MISSING — its status is MISSING with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight 0.0 — and a MISSING artifact carries no fact under POL-GEN-02, so the record contains no traffic data at all for the recommended route at the trip time. Under POL-RD-23 a reroute is justified only where a traffic advisory intersecting the recommended route and overlapping the trip window shows congestion, an incident or a closure, and a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute; the driver's statement that he 'saw it on the map' is exactly such an uncorroborated assertion.

With no traffic justification and a deviation of 1.90 km (over 1 km), row (d) of POL-RD-24 applies: the excess distance fare is refunded in full. The excess distance fare is the deviation distance times the per-km rate without surge — 1.90 km x 0.92 SGD/km = 1.75 SGD, which is the ledger's own excess_distance_fare_sgd figure — so the rider is owed a PARTIAL_REFUND of 1.75 SGD against the 6.50 SGD contested (the whole trip fare cannot be returned, as the rubric's notes confirm).

The driver's message MSG-06008-003 and the rider's reply 'ok, thanks' MSG-06008-004 do establish that the rider was informed and agreed for POL-RD-21's purposes, but that does not defeat the refund: the no-refund row (a) of POL-RD-24 requires the reroute to be traffic-justified in addition to informed-and-agreed, and this reroute is not traffic-justified, so the case falls in row (d) and not row (a). Consent to a reroute the record cannot justify does not convert it into a justified one.

This case can and should be decided by the AI rather than escalated: the contested amount is 6.50 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the AI ruling is final; neither profile carries a fraud flag; the deviation of 1.90 km is under POL-RD-25's 2.0 km figure (which is in any event not applied, as ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false); and every fact POL-RD-24 needs — the recorded distances, the route chronology, the chat and the fare components — is carried by complete artifacts at weight 1.0, so there is no open question to escalate under POL-GEN-26.

To both parties: I cannot decide this dispute on the record, so it goes to a human reviewer and the fare is held — it is neither refunded to the rider nor released to the driver.

What the record does establish. The trip ran 1.90 km longer than the recommended route — 25.10 km recorded against 23.20 km recommended on EV-TRIP-06008 — which is over POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance, and both sides accept that figure. The driver's in-app message MSG-06008-003 ('PIE got accident near Bedok, I go New Upper Changi Road then Upper Changi Road North, ok?', sent 18:42:36) was delivered to the rider before the deviation was logged at 18:45:16, and the rider answered 'ok, thanks' (MSG-06008-004, 18:43:01). On EV-CHAT-06008 the rider was therefore informed and agreed, as POL-RD-21 requires, and the driver's GPS trace (EV-GPS-06008) shows the vehicle on exactly the roads the driver announced.

The fact the record cannot establish. POL-RD-23 justifies a reroute only on actual traffic data for the recommended route at the trip time. The only such artifact, EV-ADVIS-06008-01, is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT): the platform's LTA feed request for the trip window timed out and was never retried. A MISSING artifact carries no fact (POL-GEN-02), and POL-GEN-26 names 'whether traffic justified the reroute' among the facts that force escalation when the evidence that would carry them is missing or impaired. The record is silent on traffic; it is not a finding of no traffic. The driver's assertion that he saw the accident 'on the map' is an assertion without data, which POL-RD-23 says does not by itself justify a reroute — but it is equally not proof that there was none.

Why I have not awarded the 1.75 SGD the rider seeks. The rider's argument is that the missing traffic data makes the reroute 'not traffic-justified', placing the case in POL-RD-24 row (d). I do not accept that step. It infers an outcome from absent evidence, which POL-GEN-26 forbids, and the refund matrix itself directs that a case fitting no row is escalated. If the reroute was traffic-justified, row (a) — informed, agreed, over 1 km — returns nothing; if it was not, row (d) returns the excess distance fare. I cannot tell which, so no row applies and the case escalates under POL-GEN-26.

The stakes, for the file and not as a finding. Had the case been decided, the most that could be refunded is the excess distance fare: 1.90 km x 0.92 SGD/km = 1.75 SGD (POL-RD-24, using the per-km rate of 0.92 in EV-FARE-06008), not the 6.50 SGD claimed. The claim text's premise that the fare came out higher than 'the estimate' has no figure to stand on: EV-FARE-06008 carries quoted_fare_sgd null, and its itemised lines (3.80 base + 23.09 distance + 8.64 time + 3.55 surge + 0.90 platform = 39.98) reconcile to the amount charged.

On confidence. The contested sum is 6.50 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and neither profile carries a fraud flag, so value alone would let the AI rule. But POL-RD-25 requires a confidence of 0.80 or more on a route deviation, and the decisive fact — traffic justification — rests on a missing artifact, whose weight of 0.0 supports no finding. My confidence is 0.50, below that bar, so the AI cannot rule the merits and the case must escalate.

Open question for the reviewer, recorded here rather than as a referral: obtain the LTA traffic record for the recommended PIE segment near Bedok on 2026-09-27 between roughly 18:30 and 18:46. If it shows a qualifying incident, closure or congestion (the POL-RD-23 types), the reroute was traffic-justified and, the rider having been informed and agreed, POL-RD-24 row (a) applies and nothing is refunded. ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver. I have read the trip record, the driver's GPS trace, the in-app chat, the fare ledger and the two profile snapshots. I cannot decide the money on this record, so the case goes to a human reviewer and the fare is held rather than refunded or kept.

What the record does establish. The recommended route was 23.20 km and the vehicle travelled 25.10 km, a deviation of 1.90 km (POL-RD-22, EV-TRIP-06008), which is above the 1.0 km tolerance. The vehicle left the PIE at the Bedok North Avenue 3 exit at 18:45:16 and rejoined at Loyang Avenue / Upper Changi Road North at 19:01:07. The driver told the rider before the deviation, by in-app chat: MSG-06008-003 at 18:42:36 ('PIE got accident near Bedok, I go New Upper Changi Road then Upper Changi Road North, ok?'), answered 'ok, thanks' at 18:43:01. POL-RD-21's notice requirement is therefore met and the reroute was agreed. These facts are carried by complete artifacts at weight 1.0, and I accept the driver's claims on them.

What the record cannot establish. POL-RD-23 makes a reroute traffic-justified only where traffic data for the recommended route at the trip time shows congestion, an incident or a closure. The traffic advisory for this trip, EV-ADVIS-06008-01, is MISSING (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0): the platform's request to the LTA historical traffic feed timed out and was not retried. The record is silent on whether there was an accident on the PIE near Bedok — the artifact itself records that this is not a finding that there was no traffic — and a MISSING artifact carries no fact (POL-GEN-02(3)). The driver's belief that he 'saw it on the map' is an assertion with no supporting data and, on POL-RD-23, does not justify the reroute.

Why the AI cannot rule. POL-RD-24's matrix turns on traffic justification: row (a) (no refund) needs the reroute traffic-justified; row (d) (refund of the excess distance fare) needs it not traffic-justified. Neither can be found, so no row fits, and POL-RD-24 sends a case that fits no row to escalation under POL-GEN-26 — which names 'whether traffic justified the reroute' among the facts that must be escalated when the evidence that would carry it is missing. The rider's argument that the empty record is itself proof the reroute was not justified is not accepted: silence is not a finding of no traffic, and POL-RD-23's rule about a bare assertion is not a finding about the traffic itself. An undecided limb supports neither a payment that needs the clause to hold nor a refund that needs it to fail.

The money. I accept the rider's figures — deviation 1.90 km (25.10 minus 23.20), excess distance fare 1.90 x 0.92 = 1.75 SGD (POL-RD-24, matching the ledger's excess_distance_fare_sgd), with nothing returning the base fare, the time fare of 8.64, the platform fee of 0.90 or the surge of 3.55 — but because traffic justification cannot be established I cannot award even that 1.75, and I cannot return the whole 6.50 SGD the rider asks for. The claim that the AI can decide without escalation (POL-GEN-22, POL-RD-25, POL-GEN-26) is not accepted: the fact the traffic limb turns on is carried only by a MISSING artifact of weight 0.0, so confidence is capped at 0.00 under POL-GEN-02(2), below the 0.80 POL-RD-25 requires. The amount contested, 6.50 SGD, is below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band and neither profile carries a fraud flag, but that does not cure the missing traffic record.

Open question for the reviewer: whether traffic on the PIE near Bedok around 18:45 on 27 September 2026 justified the reroute — the LTA historical traffic feed should be retried. If it did, POL-RD-24 row (a) applies (the rider was informed and agreed) and nothing is refunded; if it did not, row (d) applies and the excess distance fare of 1.75 SGD is returned. The 39.98 SGD fare is held pending that check.

ledger.claim: The platform's own recorded distances establish a deviation over tolerance on this trip: actual distance 25.10 km minus recommended distance 23.20 km is 1.90 km, which is more than the 1.0 km tolerance POL-RD-22 sets, so the deviation is over tolerance and the over-1-km rows of POL-RD-24 govern.

The driver's GPS trace confirms which route was actually taken and when — the vehicle left the recommended PIE line at 18:45:16 and rejoined it at Loyang Avenue / Upper Changi Road North at 19:01:07, travelling via New Upper Changi Road and Upper Changi Road North — but POL-RD-22 forbids re-measuring the route from the trace because a sparse trace understates its length (this trace measures only 21.24 km, below the recommended 23.20 km), so the driver cannot use the trace to argue the deviation was within tolerance; the recorded 1.90 km stands.

The reroute is not traffic-justified. The traffic advisory for this trip, EV-ADVIS-06008-01, is MISSING — its status is MISSING with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight 0.0 — and a MISSING artifact carries no fact under POL-GEN-02, so the record contains no traffic data at all for the recommended route at the trip time. Under POL-RD-23 a reroute is justified only where a traffic advisory intersecting the recommended route and overlapping the trip window shows congestion, an incident or a closure, and a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute; the driver's statement that he 'saw it on the map' is exactly such an uncorroborated assertion.

With no traffic justification and a deviation of 1.90 km (over 1 km), row (d) of POL-RD-24 applies: the excess distance fare is refunded in full. The excess distance fare is the deviation distance times the per-km rate without surge — 1.90 km x 0.92 SGD/km = 1.75 SGD, which is the ledger's own excess_distance_fare_sgd figure — so the rider is owed a PARTIAL_REFUND of 1.75 SGD against the 6.50 SGD contested (the whole trip fare cannot be returned, as the rubric's notes confirm).

The driver's message MSG-06008-003 and the rider's reply 'ok, thanks' MSG-06008-004 do establish that the rider was informed and agreed for POL-RD-21's purposes, but that does not defeat the refund: the no-refund row (a) of POL-RD-24 requires the reroute to be traffic-justified in addition to informed-and-agreed, and this reroute is not traffic-justified, so the case falls in row (d) and not row (a). Consent to a reroute the record cannot justify does not convert it into a justified one.

This case can and should be decided by the AI rather than escalated: the contested amount is 6.50 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the AI ruling is final; neither profile carries a fraud flag; the deviation of 1.90 km is under POL-RD-25's 2.0 km figure (which is in any event not applied, as ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false); and every fact POL-RD-24 needs — the recorded distances, the route chronology, the chat and the fare components — is carried by complete artifacts at weight 1.0, so there is no open question to escalate under POL-GEN-26.

The driver informed the rider of the reroute by in-app chat before the deviation and the rider agreed to it. EV-CHAT-06008 is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 and shows MSG-06008-003 from the driver at 18:42:36 — 'Hi, PIE got accident near Bedok, I go New Upper Changi Road then Upper Changi Road North, ok?' — read by the rider at 18:43:13, and MSG-06008-004 from the rider at 18:43:01, 'ok, thanks'. EV-TRIP-06008 logs route_deviation_detected at 18:45:16, so the notice preceded the point of deviation by almost three minutes and carried a brief reason. POL-RD-21's information requirement is therefore met on recorded in-app chat, and because the chat log itself confirms the rider's acknowledgment, the deviation is an agreed one and no voice-notice problem of the kind POL-GEN-26 addresses arises. The log is complete (4 of 4 entries, not truncated) and carries no objection from the rider at the time; the doubt now expressed in the claim text is a later change of position, not a contemporaneous objection.

The reroute was driven exactly along the roads the driver named to the rider, which is the use POL-RD-22 prescribes for the trace — showing which route was taken and when, not re-measuring distance. EV-GPS-06008 is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 (73 fixes, 100.0% coverage, no gap over 30 s) and shows the vehicle on the PIE until 18:44:54, then on New Upper Changi Road from 18:45:24, then Upper Changi Road North and Loyang Avenue — the identical sequence announced in MSG-06008-003 — rejoining at 19:01:07, the point EV-TRIP-06008 logs as route_rejoined. The trip record carries a single deviation event and a single rejoin event. This is not an unannounced or a wandering detour: it is one announced alternative segment, taken and left where the driver said it would be.

DISCLOSURE: EV-ADVIS-06008-01 is MISSING, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0. The fact this case turns on — whether traffic justified the reroute — cannot be established on this record, and POL-GEN-26 requires escalation rather than a finding against the driver. The platform's request to the LTA historical traffic feed for this trip window timed out and was never retried, so no traffic data for the PIE near Bedok at 18:45 is in the record at all; under POL-GEN-02(3) a MISSING artifact carries no fact, and the artifact itself records that the record is silent on traffic on the recommended route and that this is not a finding of no traffic. The driver does not contend that his own assertion satisfies POL-RD-23 — that clause says an assertion without data does not justify a reroute — but POL-RD-23 presupposes that traffic data exists and shows none; here the data does not exist, which is precisely the situation POL-GEN-26 addresses and not a case of a rule that resolves by absence. Escalation is the honest disposal: it holds the fare rather than refunding it, and the open question is narrow and runs the driver's way — if the reviewer confirms the Bedok accident, POL-RD-24 row (a) applies and, the rider having agreed, nothing is refunded.

If the judge rules rather than escalates, the amount at stake is capped far below the 6.50 SGD claimed. The deviation is 1.90 km (25.1 km actual minus 23.2 km recommended, EV-TRIP-06008, per POL-RD-22) and it exceeds the 1.0 km tolerance, so the no-refund tolerance rows (c) and (e) of POL-RD-24 do not apply and the driver does not claim them. The excess distance fare is 1.90 x 0.92 = 1.748, rounded to the cent with no surge, i.e. 1.75 SGD (POL-RD-24 and the excess_distance_fare formula), using fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd of 0.92 from EV-FARE-06008. No row of POL-RD-24 returns base fare, time fare, the platform fee or the surge on the non-deviating part of the trip, and the rider's premise of a gap against 'the estimate' has nothing in the record to stand on: EV-FARE-06008 carries quoted_fare_sgd null and its itemised lines (3.80 base + 23.09 distance + 8.64 time + 3.55 surge + 0.90 platform = 39.98) reconcile to the amount charged on rate card RC-SG-RYDEXL-2026Q3. The most that could be refunded is 1.75 SGD.
